entry: American crime drama film written and directed by [[Michael Mann]]. It follows LAPD detective Vincent Hanna, played by [[Al Pacino]], and career thief Neil McCauley, played by [[Robert De Niro]], whose pursuit of each other strains their professional and personal lives. Mann wrote the original script in 1979, based on a Chicago police officer's pursuit of McCauley. Released by Warner Bros. on December 15, 1995, it grossed $187.4 million worldwide and received critical acclaim for Mann's direction and its leads. It is considered one of the best and most influential crime films of all time. A sequel novel, *Heat 2*, appeared in 2022.

Property of matter equal to the heat that must be supplied to an object to raise its temperature by one unit. Its SI unit is the [[Joule|joule]] per kelvin (J/K), and it measures the ability of a material or system to store thermal energy. It is an extensive property. Dividing it by mass gives the [[Specific heat capacity]], and dividing it by the amount of substance in moles gives the molar heat capacity. It usually varies with starting temperature and pressure, changing sharply during a [[Phase transition|phase transition]] such as melting or vaporization. For a block of iron weighing one pound, the value is about 204 J/K near 25 °C and 1 atm, adequate for temperatures between 15 °C and 35 °C. In architecture and civil engineering, a building's heat capacity is often called its thermal mass.

Hypothesis about the ultimate fate of the [[Universe|universe]], in which it reaches maximum entropy and thermodynamic equilibrium. Also called the Big Chill or Big Freeze, it requires no particular absolute temperature, only that temperature differences can no longer perform work. The idea follows from the [[Second law of thermodynamics]]. [[Lord Kelvin]] first proposed it in 1851, extending the view that mechanical energy turns into heat. He also formulated a paradox disproving an infinitely old universe. If the universe is flat or hyperbolic, or if [[Dark energy]] is a positive cosmological constant, expansion will continue forever and the universe will cool toward equilibrium.

Parabolic [[Partial differential equation|partial differential equation]] of heat transfer, modeling how the temperature of a body changes over time. Joseph Fourier developed it in 1822 to model how heat diffuses through a region, and it is fundamental in pure and applied mathematics. For a homogeneous, isotropic medium with thermal diffusivity α, the temperature u(x,y,z,t) obeys ∂u/∂t = α∇²u. Because the Laplacian is independent of coordinate system, the equation models any homogeneous, isotropic phenomenon. Variants appear beyond heat flow: the forward Kolmogorov equation for [[Brownian motion]] in probability, and the basis of the Black-Scholes model for option pricing in [[Finance]].

Device that uses mechanical or thermal energy to transfer [[Heat]] from one space to another, cooling one space while warming the other. In winter it moves heat from cool outdoor air into a house; in summer it can reverse the flow, like an air conditioner. In the common vapor-compression design, a refrigerant releases heat indoors, then absorbs it outdoors. Heat pumps are efficient because they move heat: 1 kWh of electricity can transfer 1 to 4.5 kWh of thermal energy into a building. Heat pumps could supply over 80% of global space and water heating needs, but in 2021 they met 10%.

Branch of thermal engineering concerned with the generation, use, conversion and exchange of thermal energy between physical systems. Heat flows spontaneously from higher to lower temperature, as the [[Second law of thermodynamics]] requires, until bodies reach thermal equilibrium. Its mechanisms include conduction, the direct exchange of kinetic energy through particle collisions; convection, in which the bulk flow of a fluid carries heat, whether forced by a pump or fan or driven by [[Buoyancy]]; and thermal radiation, the transfer of energy by photons or electromagnetic waves, which can pass through a [[Vacuum]]. Phase changes and evaporative cooling also move heat. Heat transfer is a process function, so the amount transferred depends on how the process occurs. Engineers apply it in heat exchangers, insulation and power generation.

Group of thermal and metalworking processes that alter the physical, and sometimes chemical, properties of a material, most commonly metal. Heating or chilling, normally to extreme temperatures, softens or hardens the material by techniques such as annealing, case hardening, precipitation strengthening, tempering, carburizing, normalizing and quenching. Metals consist of small crystals called grains, and heat treatment controls [[Diffusion|diffusion]] and cooling within this microstructure to change hardness, strength, toughness, ductility and elasticity. Quenching heated steel in water forms hard martensite, while slow cooling forms soft pearlite. Heat treatment is also used in making [[Glass]], and heating and cooling often occur incidentally in [[Welding]].

Australian actor noted for versatile performances in independent and studio films. After roles in Australian television and film in the 1990s, he moved to the United States in 1998. His breakthrough came in the romantic comedy *10 Things I Hate About You* (1999). He received an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor for *Brokeback Mountain*, directed by [[Ang Lee]]. His performance as the [[Joker (character)|Joker]] in *The Dark Knight*, directed by [[Christopher Nolan]], won a posthumous Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor. He died of an accidental overdose of prescription drugs; his final film, *The Imaginarium of Doctor Parnassus*, was released posthumously.

Modern pagan religion modeled on the pre-Christian beliefs of the Germanic peoples. Scholars of [[Religious studies]] classify it as a [[New religious movement]]. It developed in Europe in the early 20th century and is typically polytheistic, honoring deities such as [[Odin]], [[Thor]] and [[Freyja]] in *blóts* and *symbel* toasts. Practitioners, often in small groups called kindreds or hearths, draw on historical, archaeological and folkloric evidence. Folkish groups tie the religion to a Germanic race and restrict it to white people, often with far-right views, while universalist groups are open to all. Scholarly estimates put the number of Heathens at no more than 20,000 worldwide.

Primary international airport serving London, England, and the largest of the six international airports in the London system. Founded as a small airfield in 1930, it opened as London Airport on March 25, 1946, and was renamed Heathrow in 1966 to avoid confusion with Gatwick and Stansted. It lies about 14 miles west of central London and has two parallel east–west runways and four passenger terminals. It is the main hub for [[British Airways]] and Virgin Atlantic. In 2025 it was the busiest airport in Europe, and its busiest year was 2024, with 83.9 million passengers.

Technology that controls temperature, humidity and indoor air quality in buildings and vehicles. HVAC systems provide thermal comfort through heating, cooling, ventilation, filtration and humidity control, and their design weighs energy efficiency, air quality and environmental impact. Central systems serve multiple zones through ductwork or piping, while local systems such as window units condition a single zone. HVAC often accounts for a substantial share of building energy use, often 40-60% in commercial structures. The first comfort air conditioning system was designed in 1902 by Alfred Wolff for the [[New York Stock Exchange]]. Central heating supplies heat from a boiler, furnace or [[Heat pump]] through air, water or steam, delivered by [[Convection]] and radiation.

Religious cosmological realm where deities, angels, souls and saints are said to reside, often described as the holiest, highest place. It is contrasted with [[Hell]] and the underworld. In [[Christianity]], [[Islam]] and some schools of [[Judaism]], as well as [[Zoroastrianism]], heaven is the afterlife realm where good actions are rewarded eternally. In Indian religions, heaven is Svargaloka, and souls are reborn according to [[Karma]] until they attain moksha or [[Nirvana]]. The English word derives from Middle English heven and Old English heofon, originally meaning sky. Ancient Mesopotamians pictured the sky as domes of precious stone over a flat Earth, and the planet [[Venus]] was equated with the goddess Inanna.

Genre of [[Rock music|rock music]] marked by loud, distorted guitars, emphatic beats and extended guitar solos. It developed in the late 1960s and early 1970s, largely in the [[United Kingdom]] and [[United States]], with roots in blues rock and psychedelic rock. [[Led Zeppelin]] and [[Black Sabbath]] were among its pioneers, alongside Deep Purple. In the 1970s, Alice Cooper, Kiss and Van Halen made it more accessible, and Judas Priest discarded much of its blues influence. Thrash metal reached the mainstream in the 1980s through [[Metallica]] and [[Slayer]], while death and black metal stayed subcultural. Since the mid-1990s, nu metal has incorporated elements of grunge and hip-hop. Some metal lyrics about aggression and machismo have led to accusations of [[Misogyny]].

Form of [[Water]] in which the hydrogen atoms are the heavier isotope [[Deuterium]], written D₂O. Its molecules have two deuterium atoms in place of ordinary hydrogen, making it 10.6% denser than ordinary water, with a higher melting point. Heavy water can be lethal to multicellular organisms at concentrations over 50%, while human poisoning begins only when deuterium exceeds 20% of body fluids. Its main use is in nuclear technology: as a neutron moderator, it allows [[Nuclear reactor|reactors]] to run on natural [[Uranium]], as in CANDU reactors. It is also used in nuclear magnetic resonance, neutrino detection and the production of plutonium and tritium.

Province of North China (pop., 2020: 74.6 million), surrounding the municipalities of [[Beijing]] and [[Tianjin]]. Its capital and largest city is [[Shijiazhuang]], and 96% of residents are [[Han Chinese]]. During the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, the region was ruled by the states of Yan and Zhao. The modern province was created in 1928. Five UNESCO World Heritage Sites lie within it, including the [[Great Wall of China]] and the Chengde Mountain Resort. Hebei occupies part of the North China Plain and grows wheat, cotton and [[Maize|maize]]. It has long been China's largest steel-producing province, and heavy pollution from steel output has prompted industrial upgrading.

Canonical collection of Hebrew scriptures, also called the Jewish Bible or Tanakh. Its three divisions are the [[Torah]], the Nevi'im (Prophets) and the Ketuvim (Writings). The text authoritative in Judaism is the Masoretic Text, compiled by Jewish scribes in the early [[Middle Ages|Middle Ages]] and consisting of 24 books. It is written mostly in Biblical Hebrew, with a few passages in [[Aramaic]]. The [[Septuagint]], a Greek translation made by Alexandrian Jews, includes books later identified as apocrypha and influenced early Christianity. Scholars increasingly view the text as a mix of folklore and history, with some narratives partly supported by archaeology.

Abjad script of 22 letters used to write [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] and other Jewish languages such as [[Yiddish]]. Written right to left, it has no letter case, and five letters take special final forms. It is a stylized form of the [[Aramaic]] alphabet, itself derived from the [[Phoenician alphabet]]. Originally [[Consonant|consonants]] only, it gained vowel points called niqqud, and the letters aleph, vav and yod serve as matres lectionis to mark vowels. Its letters also function as numerals from 1 to 400. Jewish sages called the square script Ashurit, or Assyrian script, because its origins lay in Assyria.

Lunisolar calendar used for Jewish religious observance and as an official calendar of Israel, alongside the [[Gregorian calendar]]. Months of 29 or 30 days begin at approximately the new moon, but 12 months total only 354 days, so a leap month is added in 7 of every 19 years. Month starts were originally set by observing the new moon. Between the years 70 and 1178 these observations were replaced by mathematical rules. Years are counted from creation in the Anno Mundi era, and AM 5787 began at sunset on 11 September 2026. It sets the dates of [[Passover]] and other holidays.

Northwest Semitic language of the Afroasiatic family and the only Canaanite language still spoken today. Natively spoken by the [[Israelites]], it remained a first language until after 200 CE and stayed the liturgical language of [[Judaism]]. It ceased to be a regular spoken language between 200 and 400 CE but survived through the Middle Ages as the language of Jewish liturgy, rabbinic literature and poetry. With the rise of [[Zionism]] in the 19th century, Eliezer Ben-Yehuda led its revival as a spoken language, and modern Hebrew became the official language of the State of Israel. Estimates of worldwide usage include over nine million speakers in 2013, and the [[United States]] has the largest Hebrew-speaking population after Israel.

City in the southern [[West Bank]], capital of the Hebron Governorate, with 201,063 residents within city limits. One of the Levant's oldest continuously inhabited cities, Hebron is one of the Four Holy Cities of [[Judaism]] and is venerated in [[Christianity]] and [[Islam]]. The Cave of the Patriarchs is the traditional burial place of [[Abraham]]. A 1929 massacre killed nearly 70 Jews, and the British then evacuated the Jewish community. Under the 1997 Hebron Protocol, most of the city is governed by the Palestinian National Authority; the Old City and Jewish settlements are under Israeli security. The Old City is a [[UNESCO]] World Heritage Site.

Metric unit of area equal to 10,000 square [[Metre|metres]], or a square with 100-metre sides, used mainly to measure land. There are 100 hectares in a square kilometre, and one hectare is about 2.47 acres. The name combines the prefix hecto- with the are, and the unit dates from the [[Metric system]] introduced in France in 1795. It is the legal unit for land deeds, agriculture, forestry and planning in the [[European Union]], South Africa, New Zealand, Australia, Canada and the United Kingdom. The United States and Myanmar use the acre instead. As of 2026, the International Bureau of Weights and Measures no longer describes the hectare as accepted for use with the SI.

French [[Romantic music|Romantic]] composer and conductor. His works include the *Symphonie fantastique*, the *Requiem*, the operas *Benvenuto Cellini*, *Les Troyens* and *Béatrice et Bénédict*, and the "dramatic legend" *La Damnation de Faust*. Expected to follow his physician father into medicine, he chose music and won the Prix de Rome in 1830, though his unconventional style divided Paris critics. He wrote the *Symphonie fantastique* after an obsession with the actress Harriet Smithson, whom he later married. His largest opera, *Les Troyens*, was never staged in full during his lifetime. He gained an international reputation as a conductor, and his *Treatise on Instrumentation* (1844) was influential in the 19th and 20th centuries, and his innovations influenced composers such as [[Richard Strauss]].

Genus of 12–15 species of evergreen climbing or creeping woody plants in the family Araliaceae, commonly called ivy. Native to Western, Central and Southern Europe, northwestern Africa and central-southern Asia, it has juvenile leaves that are lobed and climb by aerial roots, and adult leaves that are unlobed and flower. Its greenish-yellow flowers appear in autumn and provide late nectar for insects, and birds disperse its berries. *Hedera helix* is widely planted to clothe brick and [[Masonry|masonry]] walls. Introduced ivies in North America and Australia invade forests, smothering [[Tree|trees]], and several species are classed as noxious weeds in multiple U.S. states.

Spiny [[Mammal|mammal]] of the subfamily Erinaceinae, with 17 species in five genera. Native to Europe, Asia and Africa, hedgehogs were introduced to New Zealand, and none are native to Australia or the Americas. They are mostly nocturnal omnivores, eating insects, [[Snail|snails]], frogs, snakes and eggs. Their spines are hollow hairs stiffened with keratin, and they roll into a tight ball when threatened. Many hedgehogs hibernate in underground dens. Hedgehogs share distant ancestry with [[Shrew|shrews]] and have changed little in the last 15 million years. They are sensitive to stress from humans, and wildlife clinics recommend keeping captured animals in a dark, ventilated box with minimal noise.

Family of philosophical views that give priority to [[Pleasure|pleasure]]. Psychological hedonism holds that all human behavior aims at maximizing pleasure and minimizing pain, and axiological hedonism holds that pleasure is the sole source of intrinsic value. Ethical hedonism holds that people have a moral duty to pursue pleasure. Utilitarian versions seek the greatest happiness for everyone, while egoistic versions pursue one's own pleasure. Discussed by the Cyrenaics and [[Epicurus]] in ancient Greece, hedonism became central to modern thought with the rise of [[Utilitarianism]]. Jeremy Bentham proposed a calculus to measure pleasures by intensity and duration. Critics argue that it overlooks goods such as knowledge and virtue.
